Photograph: Dan Himbrechts/AAP View image in fullscreen The female passenger was killed and the male driver was taken to hospital following a car crash in Sydney’s inner west on Friday. Photograph: Dan Himbrechts/AAP Sydney NSW police officer killed ‘instantly’ after car she was travelling in crashed into tree in Redfern The marked police car was travelling with its sirens on when it hit a tree in inner-city Sydney about 1.30am on Friday Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australian Associated Press Thu 24 Sep 2026 22.17 EDT Last modified on Thu 24 Sep 2026 22.43 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A New South Wales police officer who was killed on duty when the car she was travelling in crashed into a tree in Sydney has been named as 20-year-old Mia Lay. NSW police said the marked police car was travelling under lights and sirens along Gibbons Street in Redfern when it crashed about 1.30am on Friday. The officers were responding to a reported vehicle theft at Glebe, driving with lights and sirens activated. Lay, a female constable who had been with the force for 16 months, died instantly in the crash. Mal Lanyon, the police commissioner, thanked Mia for her courage and for choosing the police for her career. “You will not be forgotten,” he said. Paramedics treated the 24-year-old male constable who was driving before he was taken to hospital in a stable condition. A crime scene has been established, and police have declared a critical incident. The NSW police watchdog said it would monitor the force’s investigation into the crash to “ensure public confidence”. The Law Enforcement Conduct Commission said it could not independently investigate the incident until NSW police finished its probe, and any coronial or criminal proceedings were over. View image in fullscreen NSW police minister Yasmin Catley says the force is ‘mourning one of its own’. Photograph: Dan Himbrechts/AAP The premier, Chris Minns, and the police minister, Yasmin Catley, said their thoughts were with the loved ones of the officer who died. “Our police officers dedicate themselves to looking after others, and today the NSW police family is mourning one of its own,” Catley said. Minns said he was also thinking of the officer injured in the crash and those who responded at the scene. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion The NSW opposition leader, Kelly Sloane, said she was “heartbroken” by the news. “(The officer) was out working while most of us were asleep, protecting the community,” she said. Nearby Regent Street remained closed in both directions between Lawson and Cleveland streets. Motorists have been advised to avoid the area, with several bus routes being diverted. https://georgiatoday.ge/france-germany-a.text: The ambassadors of France, Germany and Poland to Georgia met in Tbilisi this week to mark the 35th anniversary of the founding of the Weimar Triangle and discuss the future of the cooperation and prospects for joint action in Georgia. The German Embassy in Georgia said a working lunch hosted at the Polish residence provided an opportunity to exchange views on European affairs and cooperation in the context of regional challenges. “Even 35 years after its inception, the Weimar Triangle remains a key platform for dialogue and coordination among France, Germany and Poland,” the embassy said.

Last year Saudi Arabia put to death 356 people. Photograph: Handout Rights and freedom Saudi Arabia Saudi Arabia to execute man for being at protests and funerals when he was 15 Use of death penalty against people for crimes committed when they were children a ‘new low’, say rights groups Supported by About this content Tom Levitt Fri 16 Oct 2026 01.00 EDT Last modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 05.43 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A young man faces imminent execution in Saudi Arabia for attending protests and funerals when he was aged 15 to 17, say human rights groups, in the latest example of the kingdom’s surging use of the death penalty for non-violent crimes. Youssef al-Manasif was arrested in 2017 and accused of crimes including joining demonstrations for religious freedom by the Shia minority and attending funerals that the Saudi authorities deem to be protests. He was convicted and sentenced to death by the specialised criminal court, a secretive tribunal set up for terrorism-related cases. The charity Reprieve says Manasif was tortured and coerced into signing a false confession and only met his state-appointed lawyer for the first time in 2022 – five years after his arrest. Manasif’s death sentence has now reportedly been upheld by the Saudi supreme court, which was likely to be his last hope of avoiding execution. His family have not spoken in public about the case and could face harassment or arrest if they do so. “There is nothing they can do now but wait,” said Duaa Dhainy, a consultant for Reprieve and the European Saudi Organisation for Human Rights. Saudi Arabia has seen what activists describe as a “horrifying” surge in executions under the rule of the crown prince, Mohammed bin Salman. Last year saw a record 356 people put to death in the country. Most of those executed are foreigners convicted of minor and non-violent drug crimes . At least 17 people, who were children at the time of their alleged offences, have been executed in Saudi Arabia since 2015, according to Reprieve. Saudi Arabia issued a royal decree abolishing the death penalty for children in 2020, stating that individuals would not be sentenced to death for crimes committed when they were minors. However, it has since upheld the death penalty in a number of cases involving child defendants. In April, it executed Ali al-Subaiti , along with his uncle, Mustafa al-Subaiti, for non-lethal “terrorist” offences committed when he was 12 years old. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every fortnight Sign up to Global Dispatch Get a different world view with a roundup of the best news, features, opinion and photography, curated by our global development team after newsletter promotion The UN’s independent human rights experts have previously expressed concerns about Manasif’s case. It said Saudi Arabia should immediately halt planned executions of people convicted of offences allegedly committed when they were under 18. “They are using execution as a tool to show how powerful they are and how they can threaten anyone who does not follow their rules,” Dhainy said of the Saudi regime. “We think he should be treated as a minor and not sentenced to death as his charges relate to when he was under 18.” Human Rights Watch said executing Manasif for a non-violent crime committed as a minor would be “an unconscionable new low”. https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/actualitate/.text: George Simion a spus miercuri seara, la Digi24, că AUR va colabora în Parlament și cu PSD și cu PNL și USR, în contextul în care partidul a votat alături de social-democrați mai multe proiecte legislative și s-a înțeles cu PSD la împărțirea unor funcții în parlament și în instituții publice. Invitat să comenteze buna colaborare din parlament între PSD și AUR pentru proiecte legislative, amendamente și împărțirea unor funcții în parlament și alte instituții de stat , George Simion nu a dat un răspuns concret, dar a afirmat că formațiunea pe care o conduce va colabora și cu PSD și cu PNL-USR, pentru că AUR este partidul care „înclină balanța” în legislativul de la București. „Funcții? Al doilea partid al țării să aibă funcții în Parlamentul României? Să aibă o funcție de secretar general adjunct, să aibă anumite președinții în instituții ale statului român care depind direct de Parlament? Ce le-aș spune oamenilor este că îmi pare rău că Ilie Bolojan a votat acest Guvern, Luca Niculescu – PSD”, a declarat George Simion. „AUR nu a votat nici guvernul Veștea, nici guvernul Siegfrid Mureșan, nici Guvernul Luca Niculescu. Proiectele noastre, ca al doilea partid al țării, trebuie să prindă viață și lucrul ăsta se va întâmpla și pe mai departe”, a punctat liderul AUR. „Vom colabora și cu PSD, și cu PNL-USR, pentru că noi înclinăm balanța în Parlamentul României și vom continua să facem acest lucru, dar noi rămânem fideli principiilor noastre. De asta nu l-am votat nici pe Veștea, nici pe Luca Niculescu. Domnul Bolojan s-a îndoit cumva, s-a înclinat”, a subliniat George Simion. EXCLUSIV. George Simion îl implică pe Nicușor Dan, fără dovezi, în cazul Călin Georgescu: A dat din cap afirmativ când s-a pus problema arestării EXCLUSIV. George Simion îl acuză pe președinte că a dat ordin ca protestul AUR să nu fie autorizat: „Nicușor Dan arată ca un despot” Urmărește știrile Digi24.ro și pe Google News
